nodes.label: Operator
nodes.description: The developer/orchestrator who runs the recovery CLIs (es-merge, es-generate, demo) and launches es-view. Here they invoke es-generate to render a validated flows.json into the two shipped, openable views.

nodes.label: GenerateViews
nodes.description: Render the canonical flows.json into the two shipped views: a Graphviz flows.dot digraph (one cluster per flow, event-storming palette) and a single self-contained explorer.html with the whole model inlined. A deterministic, stateless projection: it reads the model and writes two files, mutating nothing.

tactical.explanation: Split across two layers by the refactor: src/adapters/cli/es-generate.ts (runGenerate) is the IO/CLI action, and src/application/commands/generate-views.ts (generateViews, renderDot, renderHtml) is the pure render — no fs, no argv, data in/strings out. runGenerate JSON.parses the flows file into `model` with NO try/catch and NO validation (line 26 of es-generate.ts) -- it fully trusts es-merge's output contract. repoRoot/title resolve from --repo-root/--title, falling back to model.meta.repoRoot/title then './'Event Storming Explorer' (es-generate.ts 28-29). The unified CLI's `generate` subcommand (cli.ts) now enforces the presence of <flowsJson>/<outDir> declaratively via commander's required arguments, replacing the old hand-rolled argv guard. DOT pass (renderDot, generate-views.ts): builds a local nodeById index and a DATA_TYPES filter that excludes datastore/field nodes and any edge touching them from the board + DOT; one `subgraph cluster_<flowid>` per flow, sticky per used node colored by PALETTE, dead flows dashed + greyed, node label URL='vscode://file/<repoRoot>/<path>:<line>' from the first anchor. HTML pass (renderHtml): the model is serialized with JSON.stringify(model).replace(/</g,'\u003c') (the one injection guard) and inlined as `const MODEL` alongside REPO_ROOT + PALETTE into a ~1400-line self-contained template (tabs: Flows, Gallery, Data model, Glossary, Overview). writeViews (src/adapters/fs/generator-writer.ts) does the two sequential writeFileSync calls to outDir; no mkdir (outDir must pre-exist).

anchors.note: CLI action: reads flowsFile, resolves repoRoot/title, calls generateViews + writeViews
JSON.parse(readFileSync(flowsFile)) -- no try/catch, no validation
pure render: calls renderDot + renderHtml, returns { dot, html }
modelJson = JSON.stringify(model).replace(/</g,'\u003c') -- HTML injection guard
writeFileSync(outDir/flows.dot) then writeFileSync(outDir/explorer.html)

nodes.label: The Model
nodes.description: The canonical Event Storming model (flows.json): deduped nodes plus flows, hotspots, terms, and derived meta. In THIS flow it is a READ-ONLY input -- the generator projects it into views and never mutates or re-validates it. Its invariants are enforced upstream at merge time, not here.

tactical.explanation: es-generate.ts's runGenerate JSON.parses flows.json into `model` (line 26) and reads model.meta.repoRoot / model.meta.title as fallbacks for the --repo-root / --title flags (lines 28-29). renderDot (generate-views.ts) builds its own nodeById index over model.nodes for the DOT pass; renderHtml inlines the whole model as-is for the client to index. The generator performs NO validation of its own -- it assumes the aggregate's merge-time invariants already held (see hot-generator-trusts-unvalidated-model). Unlike the merge-traces flow, this flow does not touch the explicit Model aggregate class (src/domain/model/model.ts) at all -- it works off the plain parsed JSON shape.

anchors.note: model = JSON.parse(readFileSync(flowsFile))
nodeById index over model.nodes (throws if absent)

nodes.label: Graphviz flows.dot
nodes.description: The Graphviz digraph the operator renders offline (e.g. `dot -Tsvg model/flows.dot`) or opens in a Graphviz viewer to read the whole board at a glance: one clustered subgraph per flow, event-storming-colored stickies, labeled edges, dead flows dashed and greyed. Physical storage nodes (datastore/field) and any edge touching them are deliberately excluded so the DOT stays behavioral.

tactical.explanation: Built by renderDot (src/application/commands/generate-views.ts), a pure function now separated from the CLI action; writeViews (src/adapters/fs/generator-writer.ts) persists its output to <outDir>/flows.dot. Per flow it emits `subgraph cluster_<flowid>`, computes the `used` node set from steps + edges while skipping data-type ids via isDataId, and for each used node emits a filled/rounded box colored by PALETTE[type] with fontcolor = the palette's tonal text, a truncated description tooltip, and URL='vscode://file/<repoRoot>/<firstAnchor.path>:<line>' so a Graphviz SVG's nodes deep-link into the local checkout. Node ids are namespaced `<flowid>__<nodeid>` so a shared node appears once per flow cluster. Edges whose endpoints survived the data filter are drawn with the verb as label.

anchors.note: DOT digraph header + per-flow cluster loop
used-node set excludes datastore/field via isDataId
writeFileSync(outDir/flows.dot, views.dot)

nodes.label: Interactive explorer.html
nodes.description: The self-contained, no-server interactive explorer the operator opens in a browser: the whole model is inlined as a JS constant and rendered into five tabs (Flows board, Gallery of every sticky, Data model, Glossary, Overview) with a sticky-lane board, detail panel, search, group-by pivots, and vscode:// deep links to the analyzed source. This is the primary artifact the recovery produces.

tactical.explanation: Built by renderHtml (src/application/commands/generate-views.ts). The whole `model` is serialized once (JSON.stringify(model).replace(/</g,'\u003c') to neutralize </script> injection, line 59) and inlined as `const MODEL` with REPO_ROOT + PALETTE (lines 402-404) into a ~1400-line HTML/CSS/vanilla-JS template, written by writeViews (src/adapters/fs/generator-writer.ts) to <outDir>/explorer.html. No external dependencies are referenced -- the page is fully offline. Client anchors render as `vscode://file/<REPO_ROOT>/<path>:<line>` links (client-side anchorUrl helper, line 442) that open the analyzed checkout in VS Code. The client-side rendering (sidebar grouping, board layout, gallery, glossary, data-model tab) is the same projection logic later ported into the React SPA under src/web/*; here it is baked statically into one file.

anchors.note: builds the self-contained HTML string
modelJson escaped for safe inlining into the HTML
MODEL / REPO_ROOT / PALETTE inlined into the page
writeFileSync(outDir/explorer.html, views.html)

nodes.label: Web browser
nodes.description: The operator's browser, which opens the self-contained explorer.html directly from disk (no server). It renders the inlined model and drives all interaction; outside the tool's deploy boundary.

nodes.label: VS Code
nodes.description: The local editor targeted by the vscode://file/<repoRoot>/<path>:<line> deep links baked into both flows.dot node URLs and the explorer.html anchors. Clicking a recovered concept opens the exact source line in the analyzed checkout. Outside the tool's boundary.

nodes.label: Graphviz (dot)
nodes.description: The external Graphviz `dot` renderer the operator runs over flows.dot (e.g. `dot -Tsvg`) to produce a static image of the whole board. Not bundled; the generator only emits the .dot source.

tactical.explanation: renderDot writes DOT source only; rendering is an out-of-process step the operator invokes (documented in the example README as `dot -Tsvg model/flows.dot -o flows.svg`). The emitted node URLs survive into a Graphviz SVG as clickable vscode:// links.

flows.name: Operator generates the DOT + explorer views from the validated model
flows.summary: The operator runs es-generate (or the demo wrapper) over a validated flows.json and an output directory. The tool JSON.parses the model, then in one deterministic pass renders two artifacts: a Graphviz flows.dot digraph (one event-storming-colored cluster per flow, physical datastore/field nodes excluded) and a single self-contained explorer.html with the whole model inlined and no external dependencies. Both are written into outDir; the operator opens explorer.html in a browser and can render flows.dot with Graphviz, with vscode:// deep links from either back into the analyzed source. The generator is a pure projection: it reads the model read-only, enforces none of the model's invariants, and trusts that es-merge already validated the input.
flows.trigger: Operator runs `node dist/node/adapters/cli/cli.js generate <flows.json> <outDir> [--repo-root <path>] [--title <text>]` (the unified CLI's `generate` subcommand -- cli.ts, backed by es-generate.ts's runGenerate), or `npm run demo` chains it after the `merge` subcommand (scripts/build-example.mjs:17).

hotspots.label: es-generate renders any flows.json without validating it
hotspots.description: runGenerate JSON.parses flows.json and immediately hands it to renderDot/renderHtml with no validation and no try/catch. Unlike the server's resolveModel (which re-runs the merge and throws on errors), the es-generate path performs zero checks. Combined with the merge writing flows.json even when validation fails (see hot-invalid-model-written), an operator can generate an invalid or partial model and get a silently broken/misleading explorer, or a raw crash: a missing top-level `nodes` or `flows` array throws an uncaught TypeError from renderDot's `.map`/`for...of` (lines 21 and 31), and a missing outDir throws from writeViews's writeFileSync (no mkdir). Human question: should es-generate re-validate its input (import the domain validate()/crossValidate, or at least assert the required arrays) and fail loudly before rendering, or is trusting es-merge's output contract intended? Today the two consumers of flows.json disagree on whether to trust it.

tactical.explanation: es-generate.ts:26 `const model: Model = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(flowsFile, 'utf8'))` -- no try/catch, no schema check. generate-views.ts's renderDot:21 `new Map(model.nodes.map(...))` and :31 `for (const f of model.flows)` assume those arrays exist. No import of the domain validate()/crossValidate anywhere in es-generate.ts or generate-views.ts. Contrast src/application/commands/resolve-model.ts, which throws when merged.errors.length so the server never serves an unvalidated model. No fs.mkdirSync of outDir in generator-writer.ts, so a non-existent output dir also throws from writeFileSync. The old CLI's manual argv guard (missing flowsFile/outDir -> usage + exit 2) is gone; commander's required <flowsJson>/<outDir> arguments in cli.ts now enforce that instead, which is a genuine improvement but doesn't touch the model-validation gap this hotspot is about.

anchors.note: JSON.parse with no try/catch and no validation
model.nodes.map assumes the array exists
writeFileSync with no mkdir of outDir
